<a id="terminal-ui"></a>

# Terminal UI

The terminal UI is an optional view over the same core services. It starts only when standard input and output are a terminal; otherwise it fails with `tui.no-terminal`. The CLI remains the complete automation surface.

The screen has a header with the book and the state, a structure tree, a body pane, a status line and a key hint. The view is plain text and does not depend on terminal features beyond basic terminal control.

The loop reads one command per line, so type a command and press Enter:

```text
up/down - move in the tree or body
enter - focus the body pane
e - edit the selected body
n / N - new node / chapter (prompt)
b - new block
J / K - move the selected block down / up
s / c - sync / check
r - reload
o / x - open / close the book
q - quit
```

Without a book argument the picker lists the registered books, marks open books and opens a closed book on selection. A book opened from the picker stays open in the store.

Body edits hand the terminal to the configured editor. If a change is refused, the edited text is kept in a draft file and its path appears in the status line, so no input is lost.

The interaction is deliberately line-based for the first version. Raw key input and a richer console experience are a follow-up; the TUI adds no book behavior that the CLI does not already have.

Use the TUI for navigation and small edits and the CLI for scripted work, bulk changes and CI. Both drive the same store, so you can switch at any time.
